threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it 'the Tube' instead of 'the Overground.' Everyone here knows it’s different, and it’s a tell that you’re still figuring it out.
Last night, saw a guy playing the sax on the bus to Crystal Palace. It turned into a mini concert—total strangers cheering him on.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I saw a group of kids in flip-flops and winter jackets playing football in the snow. That's Neukölln for you.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you grab a currywurst and a craft beer before hopping on a bus that’s just as unreliable as your ex. It’s a whole vibe.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s a local when they can casually name the day a street artist last painted that wall, while tourists just take selfies.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a Muni bus stuck in traffic while a street performer juggled flaming torches next to it. Only in the Tenderloin do delays become a mini show.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists don’t realize that the quietest patios are often where locals actually unwind; they flock to the loud bars instead.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their love for touristy spots; they’ll still take photos by the Sagrada Família at sunset, oblivious to the crowds.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still look for a parking space before remembering the tube runs all night. That shock when you realize there’s no car culture here.
Last night on the 35, a guy started singing '80s pop. Not well, but the whole bus joined in. Felt like an unexpected Brixton karaoke session.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I saw a toddler on a bicycle, weaving through the market stalls, while an old man haggled over the price of a pickled herring.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: You can hear spontaneous techno parties erupting in the most unexpected places, like a random courtyard or abandoned building, especially on weekends.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know they’re local if they’ve perfected the art of dodging the pigeons at Dolores Park. Tourists just stand there, frozen.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Watched a guy serenade the Muni while a pigeon danced along to the beat. Only in the Tenderloin does a weekday commute turn into a mini concert.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Most tourists think Gràcia is all about Gaudí, but the real charm is in the tiny, unmarked tapas bars where locals gather after work.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell by the way they take pictures of the same street art for the tenth time—still marveling at the details while locals have moved on.
